channel.title: GTA VI PC race - Updates
channel.description: Unofficial RSS feed of the updates log at https://vuyp.github.io/gta6-pc-race/#updates

item.title: PortWatch reports the private build omonkey taken down, hours after its developer's reported letter from Rockstar
item.description:
• PortWatch removed omonkey from its board at 18:19 UTC, saying on its owner's word that the private build has been taken down. Its code was never public, so there is nothing to check, and no notice or statement has been published. VGTimes reported earlier today that its developer said he had received a letter from Rockstar and stopped streaming. Its row here keeps its last reported status.
  • With ztrx's repository and account gone since about 17:00 UTC, two builds of victory-fork's code have gone dark today with no reason published. The mark published with the estimate asks for a takedown notice that names VIctory, victory-fork or a build of it, and GitHub's list holds none, so the estimate is unchanged. Both cases will weigh in its next review.
  • vilocity's README now gives 4 to 8 frames a second in the first room on an RTX 5080, up from 3 to 7. klbf-lab's README adds that it never publishes a build that crashed in its own tests and that its 77-minute session was stopped by choice. XCL merged 28 pull requests into its main branch with its status row unchanged.

item.title: VI-BR-PORT joins the table near the top, and ruff-lab logs 21.8 minutes without player control
item.description:
• VI-BR-PORT, a fork of victory-fork for NVIDIA cards with 8 GB, joins at stage 6. Its README, in Portuguese, reports control, the HUD and the pause menu working at 4 to 7 frames a second at 1080p on an RTX 4060 Ti, sessions of an hour without losing the graphics device, and all 25,758 of the game's shaders translating on that card, with everything in shadow black. These are its own figures and estimates from one machine. The length of those sessions places it 4th, 2 steps short of the playable bar.
  • ruff-lab's results log now holds a session of 21.8 minutes without a crash at 3.23 frames a second on average on an 8 GB Radeon RX 6600 XT with a hard disk. It says player movement does not work yet because of a controller input problem, so it stays at stage 5.
  • vilocity's README says its rainbow glitter is gone and every shader now translates, still at 3 to 7 frames a second. five-star-recomp's status page says boots now stay 5 to 7 minutes in the world, with the lit picture still wrong.
  • News check: other trackers repeat that ztrx's repository and account are gone, and none gives a reason. GitHub's list holds no new notice, and neither Rockstar nor Take-Two has commented since the build leaked.

item.title: victory-fork measures 4.5 frames a second in a play session, and the estimate moves back to under two days
item.description:
• victory-fork's README (17:28 UTC) reports a 370-second play session at 4.5 frames a second on average, against 10.3 standing still. Half the time goes to frames of about 490 milliseconds in which the card sits idle, because the game maps every streamed texture page itself, about 850 pages in a frame that streams. Two attempts to cut that cost were taken back out, one after faces came out black or red. Its speed lane now reads from its two play sessions, 4.5 on its own RTX 4070 and 7.6 on an RTX 4090 in a pull request, and it stays 3rd.
  • The estimate moves back by three quarters of a day, to midday on Fri 27 Nov. The best averages from sessions of play are 7.6 to 8.6 against the 20 the bar asks for, and the figures of 10 or more came from the lightest scenes. This replaces the check published for 22:00 UTC, and the estimate's note gives the next marks.
  • PortWatch reported at 17:26 UTC that ztrx's repository and the account that published it are both gone, with no takedown notice published. This page has had no answer from the repository since 16:57 UTC, and the reason is still not known.
  • VIniVIdiVIci moves to stage 6: its README reports the player in control on an RTX 4060 Ti at about 2 to 5 frames a second, with a 13-minute session and a dark picture. ruff-lab, asked for in issue 16 on this page's repository, joins at stage 5 with the world drawn at 3.2 to 3.6 frames a second on an 8 GB Radeon RX 6600 XT and no report of control yet. Scarlight now presents itself as a Steam compatibility tool for Linux, at 0.1 to 3 frames a second.

item.title: ztrx's repository stops answering, Belobug's fork reaches 5 to 7 frames a second, and the estimate is reviewed and held
item.description:
• ztrx's repository has not answered since 16:57 UTC, in three checks over 25 minutes while every other tracked repository answered, the last of them after GitHub closed its incident at 16:52 UTC. GitHub's published list holds no notice that names it and PortWatch still lists it, so the reason is not known: a repository made private, deleted or disabled looks the same from outside. Its row keeps its last reported status, without a link.
  • Belobug's fork now reports 5 to 7 frames a second on a Radeon RX 9070 XT, from 3 to 5: 5.4 to 6.7 standing still in a scene of 8,400 draws, less while driving. Its README puts the gain down to letting the game's submissions return before the card is done and to using game memory in place instead of copying it. Its speed lane moves to step 3 and it rises to 4th.
  • BRVIctory-ka1qux has turned the game's own ray-traced light on by default, the first public build on this page to do so. Its README says it costs 0.05 to 0.1 seconds a frame and has been checked on one open-world street only, in four runs of 5 to 11 minutes without a crash.
  • The estimate was reviewed at 17:24 UTC and held at about a day. For it: three code bases now report about 10 frames a second in early scenes, more builds and machines report every hour, and VIctory's own README says you can get into the game. Against it: those figures are best cases, victory-fork's maintainer says his are for a scene standing still and that the game's translated shaders now cost more than the layer, and no long session has averaged 10. The check published for about 22:00 UTC stands, and without a report of 15 in play or of 10 outside the first interiors from a long run by then the estimate moves a quarter of a day later. Neither Rockstar nor Take-Two has commented since the build leaked.

item.title: VIctory's own README now says you can get into the game, and victory-fork qualifies its 10 frames a second
item.description:
• VIctory's README (16:51 UTC) now opens with "Not playable yet, but you can get into the game". It says the intro cutscene plays and the opening mission is reached with the graphics fully displayed at about 1 frame a second on a Radeon RX 6700 XT: textured and lit, without ray-traced shadows or indirect light. Its picture lane moves from step 1 to step 2.
  • victory-fork's maintainer added a limit at 16:54 UTC to the figures reported here at 15:38 and 16:19 UTC: the 9.6 and 10.3 frames a second are for the scene standing still. While the camera moves the game streams assets, and about half the time goes to frames of about 490 milliseconds in which the card sits idle for about 330. The README did not say so when this page's last entry was written. Its speed lane now reads 2 to 12, and the estimate is unchanged ahead of its next routine review.
  • BRVIctory-ka1qux's README says the game's own ray-traced light now runs as an option on a Radeon RX 7800 XT: shaded buildings, trees and characters get bounced light, at about 0.05 seconds more per frame, in three runs of 5, 6 and 11 minutes without a crash. It is the third public code base to report this, after DexNom Runtime and a pull request to victory-fork, and it stays off by default.
  • Kelvaroq's README now says control of the character, the HUD and pausing are verified in play, and that heavy frames are down to 108.5 milliseconds. GitHub's incident was still open at 16:57 UTC, with Pages at partial outage, so this page may update late.

item.title: victory-fork passes 10 frames a second in its first rooms, and two more builds join the table
item.description:
• victory-fork's README (16:19 UTC) puts its first rooms at 97 milliseconds a frame, 10.3 frames a second, with three changes that are off by default. It also adds up the card's time: about 50 of 87 busy milliseconds are the game's own passes as translated, so with every pass of the layer's own removed the scene would still run at only about 20, and the translated shaders have to get cheaper too. The figure is from the first rooms, so neither mark published with the estimate is met and the estimate stays where it is.
  • Two builds join at stage 6, each on its own figures from one machine. Kelvaroq, from the account that published Palmwave, says the opening mission is playable at about 10 rendered frames a second in typical views and 7 to 8 in its heaviest scenes at 4K output on an RTX 5080, in measured runs of 5 minutes. victory-unified, which combines four forks' work, reports about 2 frames a second on an RTX 3070 with 8 GB and one session of 49 minutes 42 seconds, and that session length places it 3 steps short of the playable bar.
  • vilocity's README now gives 3 to 7 frames a second in the first room on an RTX 5080, up from 2 to 5, after leaving out the denoisers of ray-tracing passes it does not run. Its speed lane moves to step 3 and it passes BRVIctory-ka1qux.
  • TechRadar reported on 25 November that some builds have the opening chapter playable at a few frames a second, which is far from this page's bar. No statement from Rockstar or Take-Two has appeared since the build leaked. GitHub's status page has shown an incident since 15:55 UTC that affects Pages and Git operations, and two of this page's deployments have failed, so updates may arrive late.

item.title: victory-fork measures 9.6 frames a second in its first rooms, VIctory's main branch moves again, and two builds join the table
item.description:
• victory-fork's README (15:38 UTC) puts its first rooms at 104 milliseconds a frame, 9.6 frames a second, with two changes that are off by default, from about 120 that morning. It says the layer's submit thread and the card are both full, so taking time off one alone moved the frame by 0 to 7 percent, and that the console's pace of 33 milliseconds is still far off. The figure is under both marks published with the estimate, which stays where it is.
  • VIctory's maintainer pushed 82 commits to its main branch at 15:46 UTC, the first since 01:36 UTC: texture uploads made in batches and only when their bytes change, cheaper memory tracking and shader fixes. Its README still gives the world at 1 to 2 seconds a frame.
  • Two builds join at stage 6. CBL VIctory, asked for in issue 14 on this page's repository, reports a run of 27 minutes 38 seconds on an RTX 5080 at 3.6 to 6.4 frames a second by scene, ended by hand, after an earlier run crashed at 20 minutes: its own figures from one machine, and it enters 3 steps short of the playable bar. Doomsday is a private build that PortWatch says it verified with ray-traced lighting at about 3 to 5 frames a second and almost no crashes. That is PortWatch's account, not the group's own, and the code is not public.
  • VItoriaBr's README now says skin, terrain, foliage and shadows are working under a shaded stand-in for ambient light taken from Belobug's fork, at up to 6 frames a second on an RTX 5060 Ti. Its picture lane moves from step 2 to step 4 on that claim.

item.title: The standings can be filtered by system, card maker and lane
item.description:
• Each row now says which systems and graphics card makers the project or its testers report running it on. It may run on others.
  • A "Filter the table" link above the standings narrows the rows by system, by card maker and by a minimum on each lane, for example a session of 30 minutes or more. Positions keep their numbers when rows are hidden. A reader suggested both in issues 12 and 13 on this page's repository.

item.title: A private build's developer says Rockstar wrote to him, and Flamingo logs a 24-minute session at 8.6 frames a second
item.description:
• VGTimes reports that the developer of the private build listed here as omonkey says he has received a letter from Rockstar and has stopped streaming his work, while promising further updates. The letter has not been published and Rockstar has not commented. It is the first report of this kind seen here.
  • Flamingo's run log reports a 24-minute play session through the whole opening and on into the city, at 8.6 frames a second on average in the world on an RTX 4070. That is the highest average reported from a session of 20 minutes or more, from one machine and unconfirmed, and it is under the 10 the next mark asks for.
  • An open pull request against victory-fork reports the game's ray-tracing structure builder running whole through 7 minutes of play, kept off by default because it costs about 88 milliseconds a frame. VIniVIdiVIci moves from the watch list into the table at stage 5: its README reports the world at 3 to 5 frames a second on an RTX 4060 Ti, with no input tested yet.
  • Forecast review: the estimate stays at the evening of Thu 26 Nov. The afternoon has brought more builds, a session from a new game into the open world and ray tracing as an experiment, but no figure above 14 in play, and victory-fork's main code has not moved since 12:43 UTC. News check: no statement from Rockstar or Take-Two, and no notice naming another project.

item.title: DexNom Runtime runs the game's ray tracing as an experiment, and klbf-lab reaches the open world from a new game
item.description:
• DexNom Runtime's test report (14:52 UTC) says that with an experimental mode on, the game builds and walks its ray-tracing structures in the outdoor city on a Radeon RX 7900 XTX at about 1 frame a second, and that the lighting on individual objects is not yet verified. PortWatch says it saw ray-traced lighting working in the build, and moved it to first place on its own board at 14:56 UTC.
  • klbf-lab's README (14:55 UTC) reports play from a new game to the open world on its own saves: the first two missions, then free roam at about 5 to 8 frames a second while driving and walking, in the 77-minute session it reported earlier. It stays first here.
  • vilocity moves from the watch list into the table at stage 6: its README says the opening cutscenes and the first room play at 2 to 5 frames a second on an RTX 5080, with a driver timeout about 7 minutes in. AnyXboxX reports a 23-minute run without a crash on Linux on a Radeon RX 9070 XT, past the opening mission at a median of 3.7.
  • The estimate is unchanged. Ray tracing at 1 frame a second does not bring the 20 the bar asks for closer, and no report yet reaches 15 in play or 10 outside the first interiors. victory-fork's main code has not moved since 12:43 UTC.

item.title: DexNom Runtime joins the table after PortWatch ranks it second on its own board
item.description:
• PortWatch added DexNom Runtime, a fork of VIctory for AMD Radeon cards, to its board in second place at 14:34 UTC. It says it has seen the build running level with Belobug's: the open world close to the retail game, played through missions at about 3 to 4 frames a second.
  • The fork's own test report gives 3.5 to 4 frames a second indoors on a Radeon RX 7900 XTX from a saved game, with interior lighting still wrong and no session length. On this page's rule it enters at stage 6, 6 steps short of the playable bar.
  • five-star-recomp's status page says a boot ran 18 minutes in the world without losing the graphics device, once it held back the game's ray-tracing passes. Its picture of the world is still in red only.
  • VIctory-macOS reports frames in the world on an M5 Pro down from 4.5 seconds to about 2.4 to 2.9. victory-fork's main code has not moved since 12:43 UTC, and the estimate is unchanged.

item.title: VIctory-Belobug-AMD shades its stand-in light, and IGN asks Take-Two for comment
item.description:
• VIctory-Belobug-AMD's README (14:00 UTC) says its stand-in for ray-traced light is now weaker in creases and under objects, and that the game's own sun and lamp shadows work. It still reports 3 to 5 frames a second on a Radeon RX 9070 XT, says about 380 draws a frame are dropped, and says the frame is bound by the processor's work.
  • VIctory-macOS reports its current code staying in the world for over 20 minutes without freezing on an M3 Max, at 0.1 to 0.2 frames a second. Nobody has reached gameplay on a Mac.
  • News check: IGN has reported on the takedown and says it has asked Take-Two for comment. No statement from Rockstar or Take-Two has appeared since the build leaked, and GitHub's list shows no notice naming another project.
  • VIniVIdiVIci, a fork of victory-fork checked on an RTX 4060 Ti, joins the watch list at a reader's request. Its README says it has not yet published results of its own in play. The estimate is unchanged at the evening of Thu 26 Nov.

item.title: klbf-lab plays the second mission to its end, two forks join the table, and the estimate moves a quarter of a day earlier
item.description:
• klbf-lab's README (13:47 UTC) reports the opening mission and all of the second played to the end in one 77-minute session without a crash on its newest test build, on a Radeon RX 9070 XT, at about 5.2 frames a second on average and about 9 in flight. It says the game's own saves work, and that vegetation turns magenta and the ground stays very dark at night.
  • Two forks of victory-fork join the table at stage 6, on their READMEs' own figures from one machine each. Flamingo reports the first gameplay scene of a title it does not name at 9 to 12 frames a second on an RTX 4070 at reduced resolution, about 14 in its lightest view, in 15-minute runs, and enters second in the order. BRVIctory-ka1qux reports a 25-minute play session and 6.6 to 6.9 in steady open-world views on a Radeon RX 7800 XT.
  • The estimate moves a quarter of a day earlier, to the evening of Thu 26 Nov, just over a day away. Flamingo's is the second report of 10 or more in play, from a second machine after victory-perf's, which is the condition this page published at 10:36 UTC. Both come from the lightest scenes, Flamingo's newest code is at 9 to 10, and ordinary play elsewhere is 5 to 9 against the 20 the bar asks for, so the move is small.
  • What moves it next. Earlier by a quarter of a day: 15 or more in play on any machine, or 10 or more outside the first interiors from a long run. Later by a quarter of a day: these figures withdrawn or contradicted, a takedown notice naming VIctory, victory-fork or a build of it, or neither of the earlier marks reported by the review at about 22:00 UTC on 25 November.

item.title: klbf-lab's test build gets through the seaplane flight, and a second card confirms its water fix
item.description:
• klbf-lab's README (13:12 UTC) says that on its newest test build the boat, a seaplane take-off, the flight at about 9 frames a second and the water landing in the second mission all work on a Radeon RX 9070 XT. It has not yet played that mission to its end on the build.
  • It says another user confirmed the water fix on an RTX 5070 Ti, in a build of that user's own. klbf-lab stays first in the stage 6 order, 2 steps short of the playable bar.
  • victory-fork's main code has not moved since 12:43 UTC. An open pull request reports the game running 74 seconds with the builder of its ray-tracing structures switched on, where it crashed within seconds before; nothing changes on screen yet.
  • VIctory-macOS reports its current code loading into the world on an M5 Pro without freezing, at 0.2 frames a second, up from 0.1. Nobody has reached gameplay on a Mac.

item.title: Stage 6 is now ordered by a published rule, and klbf-lab moves to first
item.description:
• Until now the order inside a stage was this page's own judgement. From this check the 13 rows at stage 6 are ordered by their lanes and nothing else: fewest steps short of the playable bar on speed and stability together, then the better picture, the higher frame rate and the longer session. The key under the standings title states the rule, and each row shows its count.
  • Speed is now read as the middle of the frame rates a project reports in play, where it was the best of them, so a best-case scene no longer sets the step. victory-perf's 4.5 to 14 reads as step 3 of 6, down from 4, and VItoriaBr's 3.5 to 6 as step 2, down from 3.
  • The order today: klbf-lab, victory-fork, AnyXboxX, ztrx, VIctory-Belobug-AMD, victory-perf, omonkey, victory-amd, suri, VItoriaBr, ScarlettPort, CGBJ and VIctory. klbf-lab and victory-fork are level at 2 steps short, and klbf-lab's picture is a step better. A project that reports no run length counts as having none, which is why VItoriaBr and ScarlettPort sit lower than before.
  • The rule reads only what projects report about themselves, on different cards and scenes, and it does not count how far into the story a build has been played. Stages below 6 have no lanes and are still ordered by this page's reading.

item.title: Correction: victory-fork withdraws the 8.9 frames a second reported here, and gives 7 to 8
item.description:
• At 12:20 UTC this page reported victory-fork's first room at 6.0 frames a second by default and 8.9 with a newer draw path. At 12:43 UTC the project withdrew both figures: its README says the two runs stood in different scenes and could not be compared.
  • Its corrected figures come from one run each on an RTX 4070. At the same load a frame takes 145 ms with the newer path off and 124 ms with it on and memory copies made in place, about 6.9 and 8.1 frames a second. On screen it reports 7 to 8 in the first rooms and 10 to 12 in lighter views.
  • The same notes describe a first play session past the first rooms. It reached the open world and lost the graphics device there in about 13 minutes, with the 12 GB card out of room for new textures, and the cause is not known.
  • The estimate does not move: the gain is smaller than first stated, ordinary play is still under 10 frames a second, and nothing was withdrawn as unstable. Also in this check, ScarlettPort reports its frozen overlay fixed, still at about 4 frames a second, and VIctory-macOS reports its loading freezes on Macs fixed.

item.title: Rows at stage 6 now show three lanes: picture, speed and stability
item.description:
• Thirteen projects sit at stage 6, so each of their rows now carries three more meters. Speed is the best average the project reports in play, stability is the longest session it reports without a crash, and picture follows written steps. The key under the standings title lists them, and blue marks the steps that meet the playable bar.
  • On speed, the front of the field is at step 3 of 6, from 5 to 9 frames a second: victory-fork at 8.9, klbf-lab at 8.4 and AnyXboxX at 6.9. victory-perf's unconfirmed 9 to 14 reads as step 4. Playable asks for step 5, 20 frames a second.
  • On stability, klbf-lab and ztrx report sessions of more than an hour, and victory-fork's code and AnyXboxX pass the 30 minutes the bar asks for. On picture, VIctory-Belobug-AMD and one private build read as lit and whole, and most of the others still have black or dark shadows.
  • The lanes were suggested by a reader in issue 8 on this page's repository.

item.title: victory-fork merges a third batch of frame-rate work and measures 8.9 frames a second in its first room
item.description:
• victory-fork's maintainer merged a third batch of frame-rate work at 12:06 UTC. On the maintainer's RTX 4070 the first room averages 6.0 frames a second by default, up from 4.5 to 5 two hours earlier, and 8.9 with a newer draw path switched on, from one run each. The opening cutscene went from 3.1 to 4.2.
  • The notes say that draw path stays off by default: of eight runs with it on, one lost the graphics device 44 seconds into the world for a reason not yet found. They also say the regular dips in earlier measurements came from the test harness and not the game, and that the merged tree's whole test suite was not run.
  • The estimate stays at late on Thu 26 Nov. 8.9 is the highest figure merged so far, but it comes from one run on one machine and is short of the 10 frames a second in play, from a long run or a second machine, that this page set as its next mark. An open pull request on the same code reports 131 to 139 ms a frame by default, about 7.2 to 7.6 frames a second.
  • klbf-lab's test page reports a median of 6.6 to 8.4 frames a second in the world at reduced resolution on a Radeon RX 9070 XT, in runs of 14 minutes, and an optional frame generation mode that shows about 17 from about 8.5 rendered. This page counts rendered frames only, and its notes now say so. TuxBox's longest recorded run on Linux is now 18 minutes 11 seconds, with the opening cutscene still not appearing.

item.title: klbf-lab's boats float in a test build, and Belobug's fork draws vehicles and distant trees whole
item.description:
• klbf-lab's README, updated at 11:51 UTC, says a newer test build fixes the water physics that stopped the second mission: with only the throttle held, the boat floated and moved for over a minute before hitting the bank. The project says a full play-through comes next, and the fix is not yet in the version it recommends.
  • VIctory-Belobug-AMD's README, updated at 11:41 UTC, now lists moving vehicles as whole and distant trees as drawn, both broken before. It lists the in-game phone as broken, some draws dropped in the heaviest places, and about 33 GB of memory committed after a quarter of an hour's drive. Its frame rate is unchanged at 3 to 5 frames a second on a Radeon RX 9070 XT.
  • An open pull request on victory-fork measures a small gain on an RTX 4070, in a scene it does not name: sending fetches to a copy queue by default took the frame from 180 to 192 ms down to 174.5 ms, about 5.7 frames a second. It is not merged, and victory-fork's main branch is unchanged since 10:20 UTC.
  • keylime moves from the watch list into the table at stage 5, in 25th place, on its README's report of the intro, main menu and loading screen at 30 frames a second, with no test machine named and no outside report. VIctory-macOS now reports a dark city skyline on an M5 Pro at 0.1 frames a second and says nobody has reached gameplay on a Mac.

item.title: klbf-lab plays further into the second mission, and one more fork joins the table
item.description:
• klbf-lab's README, updated at 11:04 UTC, reports play from the opening mission into the second as far as a seaplane, in a 41-minute session on a test build without a crash, at 5.2 frames a second on average and 12.9 at peak on a Radeon RX 9070 XT. Menus, the map and the HUD now show in that build. Boats, the seaplane and the player in water behave as if there were no water, so those parts were skipped, and the project says it has found the cause and is testing a fix.
  • victory-amd, a fork of victory-fork with fixes for AMD Radeon cards, joins the table at stage 6 in 12th place. Its README reports the opening cutscene and the first room with the player moving at 2 to 3 frames a second on a Radeon RX 7800 XT, in runs of about 8 minutes, tested on one machine.
  • VIctory-macOS reports the game reaching the world on a second Mac, an M5 Pro, as a grey screen at 0.1 frames a second, and loading at 26 to 30 frames a second instead of 8 with new patches. Two projects written from scratch join the watch list: keylime reports the intro, main menu and loading screen at 30 frames a second with no picture in the opening cutscene yet, and gta-vi-astral reports the game running its loop with no 3D picture yet.
  • Forecast review: the estimate stays at late on Thu 26 Nov. klbf-lab's 12.9 is a peak and its average is 5.2, no report reaches 10 frames a second in play from a long run or a second machine, and victory-fork's main branch is unchanged since 10:20 UTC. No new takedown notice names a listed project, and the hourly news sweep found no statement from Rockstar or Take-Two beyond the notice against Leonida.

item.title: Three more public projects join the table, two of them in-game
item.description:
• klbf-lab, a build of VIctory and victory-fork, reports the player in control from the opening mission to the start of the second on a Radeon RX 9070 XT at reduced resolution: 5.7 frames a second while playing, 7.3 standing still over 72 minutes, and 74 minutes in one session without a crash. Its README calls the figures self-reported from one machine. It enters at stage 6 in third place.
  • VIctory-Belobug-AMD, a fork of VIctory for AMD Radeon cards published at 09:41 UTC, reports the world lit and textured at 3 to 5 frames a second on a Radeon RX 9070 XT, with moving vehicles broken and a flat stand-in for ray-traced light. PortWatch, whose owner reports having seen it, ranks it first on its own scale and says it looks close to the retail game. Its README says it is not playable yet. It enters at stage 6 in fourth place.
  • Port of the Americas, a Linux layer, joins at stage 5: its press-start screen, setup pages and loading screens draw, and its world is still black. five-star-recomp's status page says the opening shot's 3D world now reaches the screen through the final composite, in red only. XCL merged 35 pull requests into its main branch between 10:40 and 10:51 UTC with no change to its stated status.
  • The estimate does not move. None of the new figures reaches 10 frames a second in play, and they sit in the same 3 to 7 range as the rest of the field. They add to the evidence that the picture and stability are no longer what holds a playable build back.

item.title: victory-fork merges a measured frame-rate gain, and the estimate moves a quarter of a day earlier
item.description:
• victory-fork's maintainer merged a second batch of frame-rate work at 10:20 UTC. On the maintainer's RTX 4070 the first room went from about 3.5 to 4 frames a second to 4.5 to 5 by default, and to 6 to 7 with every new switch on. The change that lost the graphics device earlier is now in, off by default, with five runs since its fix and no loss.
  • The notes say frame-rate dips remain with no known cause, and that the merged tree's whole test suite was not run. The figures come from one machine and one room.
  • The estimate moves a quarter of a day earlier, to late on Thu 26 Nov, about a day and a half away. A measured gain merged into victory-fork is one of the conditions published at 09:17 UTC. The gain is on a mid-range card and far short of 20, so the move is small. It moves earlier again on 10 or more in play from a long run or a second machine, and later if the gain is withdrawn as unstable or a takedown notice names one of these projects.
  • Builds that take victory-fork's code are picking the work up. ScarlettPort now reports about 4 frames a second in the opening mission on an RTX 3060, up from 2.6, with a frozen overlay over the picture, and VItoriaBr reported up to 6 on an RTX 5060 Ti at 10:10 UTC.

item.title: VItoriaBr reports up to 6 frames a second, and PercyScarlett reaches the opening scene
item.description:
• VItoriaBr's README, changed at 10:10 UTC, reports the open world at 3.5 to 6 frames a second on an RTX 5060 Ti with no driver timeouts, where it gave about 3 before. It had merged victory-fork's 07:30 frame-rate work and several community fixes from 09:31 UTC. It is the first tracked build to publish a gain since that work landed, on a mid-range card, and it is still below the 7.6 measured in a long run on an RTX 4090.
  • PercyScarlett released a v1.0 whose runtime is now built on VIctory, victory-fork and ScarlettPort. Its README says it reaches the opening scene of a title it does not name, lit and textured, at about 2 to 3 frames a second on an RTX 2060 SUPER at reduced resolution, and that speed is far from playable. It says nothing about control there, so it stays at stage 5 and moves to the top of that group, 11th.
  • The estimate does not move. Neither figure reaches 10 frames a second, nobody has confirmed victory-perf's, and victory-fork's own main branch has not moved since 07:30 UTC. The conditions published at 09:17 UTC stand.
  • News check: no statement from Rockstar or Take-Two since the build leaked, and no notice naming another project. VideoCardz has picked up the story, reporting gameplay at 2 to 5 frames a second in unofficial builds and saying projects are moving into private development after the takedown. Of the public repositories this page tests, all but Palmwave still answer.

item.title: Estimate held at its mid-morning review
item.description:
• The mid-morning review leaves the estimate at early on Fri 27 Nov. This was the check for moving it a quarter of a day later if speed had not moved. It has started to: victory-fork merged its first frame-rate work at 07:30 UTC, and its notes name the cost that remains and a change that more than halves it but is not yet stable.
  • It does not move earlier either. Nothing measured in a long run has beaten about 7.6 frames a second since 22:15 UTC on 24 November. victory-perf's 9 to 14 in interiors is still one unconfirmed report, the only other reduced-resolution measurement is 6.1 to 6.4 on an RTX 3090 Ti, and XCL has reported neither control nor a longer run.
  • What moves it next. Earlier by a quarter of a day: a second report of 10 or more in play, a confirmation of victory-perf's figures by someone else, or a measured gain in frame time merged into victory-fork. Later by a quarter of a day: those figures withdrawn or contradicted, or none of the three by the review at about 13:30 UTC.
  • News check: nothing new. Neither Rockstar nor Take-Two has commented since the build leaked. Today's coverage, heise's included, reports the Leonida takedown from the notice GitHub published. No notice names another project, and no outlet has covered or tested victory-perf.

item.title: VIctory-macOS reports the game world on screen on a Mac
item.description:
• VIctory-macOS's README, changed at 08:25 UTC, says that in a later run on one tester's M3 Max the game world appeared on screen before the game's own watchdog stopped it, with frames taking up to 28 seconds while shaders compiled. It is this project's first report of the world on screen on a Mac. It says nothing about control, so it stays at stage 5 and moves up one place to 13th, and the README still says the game is not playable on the Mac.
  • Nothing has moved at the front. victory-fork's main branch is unchanged since 07:30 UTC, VIctory's since 01:36 UTC and XCL's world branch since 07:45 UTC. New pull-request measurements on victory-fork stay at about 4 frames a second on an RTX 3090 Ti, and victory-perf's figures are still unconfirmed.

item.title: ScarlettPort joins the table, and a second reduced-resolution measurement comes in under 7 frames a second
item.description:
• ScarlettPort, a public build of victory-fork's code that this page had not listed, reports the lit world at about 3 to 4 frames a second on an RTX 3060 at reduced resolution, with the keyboard walking the character. Its README does not name the title and says nobody has played a session end to end. It enters the table at stage 6 in sixth place. victory-perf credits it for some of its code.
  • A victory-fork pull request measured the game's lower-resolution mode on an RTX 3090 Ti: 6.1 to 6.4 frames a second, steady, in the opening mission, against 4.7 to 4.8 at full resolution. That supports the direction of victory-perf's report but not its 9 to 14, which nobody else has confirmed. The estimate does not move.
  • News check: neither Rockstar nor Take-Two has commented since the build leaked. TweakTown's report that the Leonida takedown is confirmed rests on the notice GitHub published, and no notice names another project. GameGPU describes footage, credited to a post on X, of boat gameplay on open water at 3 to 5 frames a second, which matches what builds listed here report. No outlet has tested or covered victory-perf.
  • XCL's unmerged world branch gained 17 commits on memory mapping and device handling, with no new frame rate, run length or word on control. victory-fork's main branch has not moved since 07:30 UTC and VIctory's since 01:36 UTC.

item.title: A new fork reports 9 to 14 frames a second in interiors, and victory-fork merges its first frame-rate work
item.description:
• victory-perf, a fork of victory-fork published on the morning of 25 November, reports the opening mission's interiors under player control at 9 to 14 frames a second on an RTX 4070 SUPER, and 4.5 to 6.5 in heavy scenes. The figures are its maintainer's own, from one machine at reduced resolution, with no run length given and shadows lit by stand-ins, and its heavy-scene figure matches what AnyXboxX already reports on the same card. It enters the table at stage 6 in fifth place until someone else confirms it. It calls those scenes playable, which they are not by this page's bar of 20 frames a second held for 30 minutes.
  • victory-fork's maintainer merged the fork's first frame-rate work at 07:30 UTC. One processor-side pass fell from 70 to 220 ms a frame to about 3, but the frame is still 250 to 380 ms on an RTX 4070 because, in the README's words, "the card is the limit now". A change the maintainer tried cut the card's time from 100 to 150 ms a frame to 35 to 80, lost the graphics device twice and was left out.
  • The estimate stays at early on Fri 27 Nov. These are the first signs of speed moving since 22:15 UTC on 24 November, but the best figure from a long run is still about 7.6 frames a second and the new ones are unconfirmed. A second report of 10 or more in play, or a measured gain in frame time merged into victory-fork, would move it earlier. The mid-morning check will weigh these reports before moving it either way.
  • Also on 25 November: VIctory-macOS reports the picture showing on one tester's M3 Max as far as the opening title card, where the game froze, and enters the table at stage 5. five-star-recomp says the opening shot's 3D world now draws into an off-screen buffer and does not reach the screen yet. TuxBox published a second machine's run record, in which the game reported itself running for 12 minutes 45 seconds with loading artwork on screen before a crash.

item.title: Leonida Continued joins the table, and the estimate holds at its review
item.description:
• Leonida Continued, a continuation of the halted Leonida that this page has listed under Watching as leonida (ubiquitarianism), changed its README at 07:04 UTC. It now says the game boots on Windows and on Linux through Proton, shows the launch movie, the first-run pages and the landing prompt, which respond to a controller, then runs the story load to its end and enters what it calls the world phase.
  • By its own account no frame of the world has been verified on any test machine and nothing is playable. Its test report covers about 80 starts on a Linux machine with an RTX 4070 and runs on a Windows machine with an RTX 4070 Ti, and lists a lost graphics device at the start of the world among the things that stop it. It enters the table at stage 5, recognisable picture.
  • Forecast review: the estimate stays at early on Fri 27 Nov. No speed gain has been merged in the VIctory family, the best figure measured in play is still about 7.6 frames a second, and new measurements in victory-fork pull requests come in at about 4.3 at best on an RTX 3090 Ti and an RTX 4090. The check for moving it a quarter of a day later comes mid-morning in Europe, at the review due at about 09:30 UTC.
  • News check: nothing new. Neither Rockstar nor Take-Two has commented since the build leaked, no outlet has confirmed the reported notices over footage with Take-Two, and GitHub's list shows no notice naming another project. Palmwave's repository is still not answering.

item.title: victory-fork: the first room renders right, and the frame rate is where it was
item.description:
• victory-fork's maintainer merged another batch at 06:46 UTC. The README now says the first room renders right on the test machine, with walls, textures, people and lamps, at 190 to 450 ms a frame, which is 2 to 5 frames a second. In its words, the picture work has caught up and the frame rate has not.
  • The notes credit two fixes taken from VIctory and from pull requests, and say the processor now compares 25 MB a frame for shader writes where it compared 550 to 710 MB. A change that saves 3.1 GB of the card's memory ran on a card for the first time and stays off by default. One five-minute run had no device loss, and the merged tree's test suites were not run.
  • Its headline status still says 2.5 to 4 frames a second with shadowed areas black. The best figure measured in play is unchanged at about 7.6 frames a second, so the estimate does not move.

item.title: XCL corrects its figure: about 5 frames a second in the world, not 14
item.description:
• XCL's README, changed at 06:23 UTC, now gives about 5 frames a second in the 3D world on an RTX 5090. Its commit note says the 14 it published at 04:53 UTC was the average of a whole 5-minute run with menus and loading included, and that the world ran at 5 to 6. It has lowered its own progress estimate from about 65 to about 60 percent.
  • This page reported the 14 at 05:01 UTC as a whole-run average and did not count it as a frame rate in play. XCL's world figure now sits alongside the VIctory family's 3 to 7.6. The rest of its report stands: the picture of the world is incomplete, runs there are short, and it does not say whether the player has control.
  • Elsewhere: victory-fork's main branch has not moved since 05:44 UTC, and VIctory's has not moved since 01:36 UTC. No new takedown notice has appeared in GitHub's list.

item.title: Take-Two is reported to be sending takedown notices over footage of unofficial builds
item.description:
• VGTimes and Twisted Voxel report, citing a post on X by the reporter Ben, that Take-Two is sending takedown notices over social media posts that show footage of unofficial PC builds. By VGTimes' account, one notice says the port is being developed from leaked copies of Rockstar's files and that the footage contains Rockstar's characters, environments and other material.
  • Neither report names a platform, a number of notices or a project, and neither carries a statement from Take-Two. It is the first reported action since the notice against Leonida. No new notice has appeared in GitHub's public list.
  • Neither company has commented since the build leaked. Before launch, Take-Two's chief executive said piracy would be met with legal and technical measures, and called unofficial PC ports made with AI a creative concern more than a financial one.
  • Projects: XCL's world branch has 12 more commits and no new figures. Two victory-fork pull requests report every ray-traced shadow program now translating, which is not yet ray-traced lighting in the game. Speed is unchanged.

item.title: victory-fork's main branch gets memory fixes; no change in speed
item.description:
• victory-fork's maintainer merged memory fixes at 05:44 UTC. A write to a memory page that the game shows at several addresses now reaches every copy of it, which the notes say happened 0.8 to 1.0 million times in a five-minute run. The first room now has its walls in the later frames of four runs out of four, against two of five before.
  • The notes report five 5-minute runs on an RTX 4070 without a device loss and give no new frame rate. They say the test card's memory is full from the first frame of the world, and that a fix for it is written but switched off and not yet run on a card.
  • Nothing else moved. VIctory's main branch is unchanged since 01:36 UTC, XCL's world branch is still unmerged, and the best figure measured in play is still about 7.6 frames a second.

item.title: Estimate reviewed and held at about 2 days; testers' reports back XCL's route into the world
item.description:
• Routine review of the estimate at 05:22 UTC: unchanged at about 2 days. XCL's report adds a second, independent route into the game's world, but it gives no frame rate in play, no player control and no long runs. In the VIctory family, the best figure measured in play has been about 7.6 frames a second for over seven hours.
  • A community-run board that tallies testers' reports on XCL's pull requests, last updated at 00:44 UTC, lists five reports of the world on screen and one of a tester playing by hand at about 6.9 frames a second in a short run. The board says these counts are not confirmed.
  • What would move the estimate: earlier if XCL reports control, a frame rate in the world or a longer run, or if a speed gain is merged in the VIctory family; later if neither has happened by mid-morning in Europe.
  • News check: no statement from Rockstar or Take-Two, no takedown notice naming another project, and no press coverage yet of XCL's report or of builds past the opening mission.

item.title: XCL reports its 3D world, at 14 frames a second on average over a short run
item.description:
• XCL's README, updated at 04:53 UTC, says that with a branch not yet merged the newer retail game it does not name goes on from its menus into its 3D world on an RTX 5090. It gives 4,307 frames in a 300-second run, which is 14 frames a second on average, and about 5 in the heaviest scene.
  • The README does not split that run between the menus, which run at 30 frames a second, and the world, so 14 is not a frame rate in play. It calls the game not playable: the picture of the world is incomplete, with its minimap and other mesh pipelines refused, and it does not keep running there for long. It does not say whether the player has control.
  • XCL is a separate code base from VIctory and its forks, so this is a second route into the game's world. It stays at stage 5 here until it reports control, and moves ahead of five-star-recomp.
  • The estimate is unchanged for now and is due a routine review at about 05:30 UTC. The best figure measured in play is still about 7.6 frames a second, from the VIctory family.

item.title: Speed work in the pull-request queues: a large gain on a synthetic test, smaller ones measured in the game
item.description:
• An open pull request on victory-fork changes how the layer tracks the memory the game writes, and reports a drop from 390 ms to 9.8 ms a frame on an idle RTX 4090. That figure comes from a test program its author wrote, not from the game: the author says no game files were on the test PC. Its effect on the game has not been measured.
  • Measured in the game: an open pull request on VIctory cuts the graphics time of a world frame on an RX 9070 XT under Proton from 600 to 720 ms down to 150 to 310 ms, and one on the fork takes an RTX 3070 laptop card in Series S mode from 353 ms to 305 ms a frame.
  • None of these is merged, and none is a new top speed: the best measured figure in play is still about 7.6 frames a second. News check at 04:20 UTC: no statement from Rockstar or Take-Two, and no new takedown notice.

item.title: XSXEmu starts the game's code on a Mac without Wine; correction on TuxBox's stage
item.description:
• XSXEmu's README now says the game's own code runs under Rosetta on Apple Silicon, starts its worker threads and opens its archives. It has not created a graphics device, run a shader or produced a frame, and it says no game is playable. It stays on the watch list.
  • Correction: the 02:09 UTC update said TuxBox stays at stage 4. TuxBox has been at stage 5 on this page since 23 November, when it showed the player-selection prompt, and the standings showed stage 5 throughout. The earlier line is fixed.
  • Nothing new on speed. victory-fork's main branch has not changed since 03:19 UTC, and VIctory's has not changed since 01:36 UTC. More than 510 pull requests have now been opened against the fork, and a new one reports and fixes a fault that ran parts of the ray-tracing structure builder up to 64 times more than asked.

item.title: victory-fork's main branch moves again; estimate reviewed and held at about 2 days
item.description:
• victory-fork's maintainer merged texture fixes at 03:19 UTC, the first change to its main branch in two hours. The notes say the first room now shows its walls and the characters' textures on a first launch, and put speed at about 3 to 5 frames a second. They add that more than half of the card's texture memory is held for detail levels the game has not loaded, which is the next job.
  • Routine review of the estimate at 03:30 UTC: unchanged at about 2 days. Stability has three reports beyond the bar, so speed is the gap. The best measured figure in play has been about 7.6 frames a second for over five hours, most of them overnight in Europe, while more than 500 pull requests have now been opened against the fork. That is too short a pause to move the estimate later, and nothing has happened to move it earlier.
  • One clue on speed for common cards: an open pull request on the fork measures the graphics time per frame in the first room at about three times higher on an 8 GB card once its texture memory runs out.
  • Press: no statement from Rockstar or Take-Two has appeared in any coverage found. The Verge reported the Leonida takedown on 24 November, and by Make Tech Easier's account it names VIctory and its forks as the projects in front. Notebookcheck relays unverified Reddit claims that more Discord servers have been removed.

item.title: Scarlight narrows to Linux on AMD and restates its speed; a fork joins the watch list
item.description:
• Scarlight's README now describes it as a port for Linux on AMD RX 9000 cards first, and says it does not support NVIDIA cards or native Windows. Its candidate build, on victory-fork's code, shows the opening mission's world lit at 2 to 3 frames a second at best on an RX 9070 XT, with many runs at 1 to 2. The earlier README said about 1 to 4. The build is not merged into its main branch.
  • Added to the watch list: project-flamingo, a fork of VIctory that Scarlight's README points NVIDIA and Windows users to. Its README still carries VIctory's status from 23 November and reports no results of its own.
  • An open pull request against victory-fork reports all 52 programs of the game's ray-tracing structure builder translating on an RTX 3060 laptop card, up from 49. Its author says the builder then writes outside its buffers and the game faults, so ray-traced lighting is still missing.
  • PortWatch now ranks ztrx first on its board, saying the build has not crashed between the opening mission and the second. Speed is unchanged everywhere: about 7.6 frames a second at best in play.

item.title: AnyXboxX's maintainer sees 7 to 8 frames a second in cutscenes
item.description:
• AnyXboxX's README now says its maintainer saw a steady 7 to 8 frames a second during cutscenes, with peaks at 9, read from the window caption on an RTX 4070 SUPER. In one scripted run the medians measured from the log were lower, at 2 to 3 frames a second depending on the scene.
  • These are cutscene figures, and the two methods disagree. Its measured figure for the world under player control is unchanged at 5.3 to 6.9, so the top measured speed in play stays at about 7.6 frames a second and the estimate does not move.
  • Nothing else changed in status. victory-fork's main branch has not moved since 01:22 UTC while more than 470 pull requests have been opened against it, VIctory's main branch has not moved since 01:36 UTC, and Palmwave remains unreachable.

item.title: AnyXboxX relays a report of the first two missions completed
item.description:
• AnyXboxX's README now says a contributor played for about 45 minutes at about 2 frames a second and completed the first two missions. The maintainer relays the report and did not measure it from the project's own logs.
  • The maintainer reports every cutscene playing in full, and measures 5.3 to 6.9 frames a second on an RTX 4070 SUPER with its newest mix of victory-fork and fifteen of that project's pull requests. The mix no longer needs the Microsoft library it tried earlier. Ray-traced lighting is still off, and some graphics are missing in places.
  • It is the furthest into the game that any public project has reported. Speed at the top is unchanged: about 7.6 frames a second at best, against the 20 that playable needs, so the estimate stays where it is.

item.title: TuxBox gets into the story intro on Linux
item.description:
• TuxBox, which is not built on VIctory, reports a Linux run under Proton getting into the story intro by the game's own state after 9 minutes 41 seconds, then crashing. Until now it had stopped at the player selection prompt.
  • It says the game is not playable: many shaders are unsupported, and the picture, input and frame times in the intro are not yet checked. It stays at stage 5 here, where it has been since it showed the player-selection prompt on 23 November. This line first said stage 4 and was corrected at 04:00 UTC on 25 November.
  • No new speed figures elsewhere. More than 430 pull requests have now been opened against victory-fork, whose main branch has not changed since 01:22 UTC.

item.title: VIctory's main branch gets a speed change; correction on palmetto's origins
item.description:
• VIctory's maintainer merged a change at 01:36 UTC that stops the runtime re-checking memory the game's shaders did not write. Its notes put the old cost at 0.45 to 0.7 seconds of a 1.5 to 1.7 second frame in the opening cutscene. The README's figure of 1 to 2 seconds a frame is not yet updated.
  • Correction: palmetto's commit history, public again since about 01:45 UTC, says the repository descends from the project network that received Take-Two's notice, and that references to the game and to that project were removed in response. This page said at 22:22 UTC that its files did not show that origin.
  • five-star-recomp reports most of the opening cutscene's 3D passes now running. Its 3D world is still not visible, and long runs end in a GPU hang.
  • Open pull requests on victory-fork and VIctory report fixes that let the game's ray-tracing structure builder run on NVIDIA cards and that restore material colours that came out black. Neither is merged.

item.title: A public build reports the whole opening mission played, in a session of over 90 minutes
item.description:
• ztrx, a build of victory-fork's code published at 01:11 UTC on 25 November, reports in its README the opening mission playable from start to finish on an RTX 3050 with 8 GB, in one session of more than 1 hour 30 minutes without a crash. It runs at 1 to 3 frames a second, and anything in shadow is black.
  • It is the first public code to make that claim and the longest session reported by anyone. PortWatch, which first listed it as a private build, says it verified the build going on into the next mission.
  • A second public build of the same code, VItoriaBr, joins the standings. Its README reports the opening scenes at about 3 frames a second on an RTX 5060 Ti and says the world is not yet playable, while PortWatch reports its live stream reaching the second mission at up to 4 frames a second.
  • victory-fork's main branch now runs at about 4.3 frames a second on an RTX 4070 by default, up from about 2.5, and lights its first room for the first time. The estimate moves in by a quarter of a day, to about 2 days: stability now has two long reports, and speed is the only gap left.

item.title: Estimate reviewed and left at about 2½ days
item.description:
• The estimate was reviewed at 01:05 UTC on 25 November and is unchanged: about 2½ days, around midday on Fri 27 Nov. The highest reported rate has not moved since 22:15 UTC, about 7.6 frames a second on an RTX 4090, while mid-range cards have caught up to 6 or 7. Playable needs 20.
  • PortWatch now says it has verified one private build playing through the opening mission into the next, at about 2 frames a second with poor rendering. That speaks to how well the game runs, not how fast, so it does not move the estimate.
  • No takedown notice names a front-runner. Palmwave's repository has been unreachable for nearly three hours, for reasons that are not known.

item.title: PortWatch reports private builds getting past the opening mission
item.description:
• PortWatch's owner reports that several private builds now play through the opening mission and load the next one, the furthest into the story anyone has reported. The report names no builds and cites no recordings, and says most appear to build on victory-fork.
  • By the same report most of them still render the world badly and vehicles mostly do not work, so the next mission cannot be played properly. PortWatch has not changed its scores, and no public project claims this.
  • victory-fork's main branch gained a fix for characters' faces and hair that came out black or pale in about three launches of four. The cause was textures uploaded before the game had filled them. Its README is unchanged.

item.title: VIctory merges about 130 pull requests, and Scarlight shows a lit picture on Linux
item.description:
• VIctory's maintainer merged about 130 pull requests into its main branch between 00:20 and 00:23 UTC on 25 November, the first movement there in nearly three hours. Its status line is unchanged: the world is drawn at 1 to 2 seconds a frame, unlit. The lighting and speed changes this page has reported from its open pull requests were not in the batch.
  • victory-fork's main branch changed for the first time since 20:45 UTC, taking two contributors' branches: a fix for AMD cards and support for more shader instructions. Its README is unchanged.
  • New entry: Scarlight, based on VIctory and aimed at AMD cards on Linux. Its README reports the opening scenes lit at about 1 to 4 frames a second on an RX 9070 XT under Proton, on a branch built on victory-fork. Its main branch still shows a mostly black world.
  • Decrypt reports that Rockstar did not respond to its request for comment on the removal of Discord servers. No outlet carries a statement from Rockstar or Take-Two.

item.title: AnyXboxX measures up to 7.1 frames a second with an optional mode
item.description:
• AnyXboxX added an optional mode that hands texture layout to Microsoft's own library, which the user must supply from a development kit and which is not in its repository. With it the maintainer measures 5.4 to 7.1 frames a second on an RTX 4070 SUPER, against 5.1 to 5.6 without, over about 3 minutes 40 seconds with no device loss.
  • The highest rate reported anywhere is still about 7.6 frames a second, on an RTX 4090 in an open pull request on victory-fork. More than 280 pull requests have now been opened against the fork, whose own main branch is unchanged.

item.title: AnyXboxX's newest mix gets the indirect-light shaders running
item.description:
• AnyXboxX now runs victory-fork with eight of that project's open pull requests. The added one makes the two shaders behind the game's indirect light translate, the ones without which everything outside direct light stayed black, and its maintainer reports their pipelines created and bound in game. Its notes do not yet claim a picture with lit shadows.
  • It measures 4.8 to 5.4 frames a second on an RTX 4070 SUPER, over about 4 minutes 20 seconds without a device loss. Ray-traced lighting is still absent.
  • An open pull request on victory-fork cuts a frame with the ray-tracing structure builder switched on from 3.3 seconds to 0.55 seconds on an RTX 5080. More than 250 pull requests have now been opened against the fork, whose own main branch is unchanged.

item.title: An 8 GB card reaches 6 to 7 frames a second in a pull request on the fork
item.description:
• An open pull request on victory-fork reports 5-minute runs in the world on an 8 GB graphics card at about 155 milliseconds a frame, 6 to 7 frames a second, up from 4 to 4.5, with no crash. It is the author's own measurement and is not merged.
  • That is close to the 7.6 frames a second reported on an RTX 4090 an hour earlier. More than 210 pull requests have now been opened against the fork, whose own main branch has not changed in effect since 20:45 UTC.
  • PC Gamer's explainer on the race, published at 21:47 UTC, says a recompilation could run within days and warns that many circulating clips look fake. It quotes no statement from Rockstar or Take-Two.
  • XValkyrie published a bundled copy of the VIctory engine at about 23:00 UTC and had removed it from its history 20 minutes later.

item.title: A 30-minute run is reported on the fork, and the estimate moves in to about 2½ days
item.description:
• An open pull request on victory-fork reports a 30-minute run in the world without an error or crash on an RTX 4090, at about 132 milliseconds a frame, or about 7.6 frames a second. It is the author's own measurement, the change is not merged, and it does not say how much of the run was under player control.
  • It is the longest session and the highest frame rate reported so far. Playable here needs 20 frames a second for 30 minutes, so the gap left is speed, and the estimate moves in by a quarter of a day.
  • Other open pull requests on the fork report the world drawing lit on an AMD RX 9070 XT, the lower-resolution Series S mode drawing the opening cutscene on an 8 GB RTX 3050 at 0.4 to 1.2 seconds a frame, and 36 of 40 ray-tracing programs translating on an RTX 5080.
  • PortWatch lists a new private build, suri, built on victory-fork: about 3 frames a second in the first scene, with a picture PortWatch calls close to the retail game. It joins the standings here as a private build, on PortWatch's word.

item.title: Correction: palmetto is back, with a new history
item.description:
• palmetto's repository answered again by 22:17 UTC, after about 25 minutes offline. Its history was replaced: five commits starting at 22:07 UTC where there had been 37, with folders renamed. Its link here is restored.
  • Its reported state is unchanged: the title boots, executes its draws and presents frames in its own window, and the picture is black.
  • This page had called it a continuation of Leonida, following a community list. The project's own files do not say that, so the label is removed.

item.title: Palmwave stops answering; ray-tracing and lighting fixes arrive as pull requests
item.description:
• Palmwave's repository stopped answering between 21:52 and 22:17 UTC. No published takedown notice names it and the reason is not known. palmetto's return shows that a repository can go quiet without a takedown.
  • An open pull request on victory-fork reports four of the five shadow-ray programs and the ray-tracing structure builder now translating on graphics cards where they had been kept off. It claims no picture yet, and the fork's README is unchanged.
  • An open pull request on VIctory traces the black, unlit world on NVIDIA cards to buffer reads that return zeros, and proposes a fix. It is not merged.
  • Tom's Hardware, heise online and Dexerto now cover Leonida's shutdown. Tom's Hardware and tbreak quote no statement from Rockstar, Take-Two, Discord or GitHub, and tbreak, citing Decrypt, reports a GTA VI modding Discord server removed and others locked down. GitHub published three more takedown notices, none about these projects.

item.title: VIctory's own code now shows the world, and the fork is reported on AMD cards
item.description:
• VIctory's README, updated at 21:36 UTC, now says the first mission's world is drawn and shown, with streets, buildings, vehicles and characters, at 1 to 2 seconds a frame. Surfaces are unlit and some geometry is missing. It lists nearly all of the world's shaders as translated.
  • AnyXboxX now runs victory-fork with seven of that project's open pull requests added. Its maintainer measures about 5.4 frames a second on an RTX 4070 SUPER and calls it the best picture so far. An earlier mix reached about 6.6 with a setting since turned off, after a report that it makes characters' skin disappear.
  • Open pull requests on victory-fork report it on AMD cards for the first time: 15 minutes in the first scene at 3.4 to 4.3 frames a second on an RX 7800 XT, and the world drawn on an RX 7900 XT. These are their authors' own measurements. One measures 5 to 8 seconds a frame under Linux.
  • palmetto's repository stopped answering at about 21:50 UTC. Its last commit, at 21:29 UTC, added a content policy and a contact path for rights holders. No published takedown notice names it, and the reason is not known.

item.title: Palmwave drops its XCL-based code for a renamed copy of the fork
item.description:
• At 21:12 UTC Palmwave replaced its main branch with a single commit whose files match victory-fork's one for one, with the names changed. Its README now repeats the fork's status table and figures, and names neither VIctory nor the fork.
  • Its XCL-based work, which an hour earlier had drawn the first mission's world into its buffers, is no longer on that branch.
  • It gives no measurements of its own on the new code, so it moves from the standings to the watch list.

item.title: The press reports the Take-Two notice; five-star-recomp's cutscene reaches 30 frames a second
item.description:
• GameRiv has reported GitHub's publication of the Take-Two notice against Leonida and its forks. It quotes no statement from Take-Two, Rockstar or GitHub.
  • five-star-recomp now plays the opening cutscene's art, credit cards, dialogue and sound at a steady 30 frames a second, up from about 1.5, after removing a slow memory query from its busiest code. The cutscene's 3D world does not draw yet.
  • XCL merged a fix for a freeze about 180 seconds into the world. Its status line is unchanged.

item.title: Correction: the build listed as hyphennn is the fork itself, now named victory-fork
item.description:
• PortWatch now says the private build it listed as hyphennn is the fork's own, shown on its developer's live streams. The separate entry added here at 20:51 UTC is withdrawn and merged into the fork's.
  • The fork has been renamed from victory-gta6 to victory-fork. Its old address redirects.
  • PortWatch reports those streams showing the first gameplay scene with ray-traced lighting, detailed textures and hair at about 3 frames a second. The fork's README still lists shadows as black.

item.title: Longer and faster runs on the fork; Palmwave draws the world
item.description:
• AnyXboxX now measures up to 5.4 frames a second on the fork, on an RTX 4070 SUPER. Its notes relay a third-party report of 21.5 minutes without a fault on an RTX 4060 Ti, which neither AnyXboxX nor this page has checked.
  • Palmwave, on XCL's code, now draws the first mission's world into its internal buffers: street, ground, trees, people and a car, shown through a debug view under a fixed light. The picture the game presents is still almost one dark colour, at 2 to 5 seconds a frame, with several passes patched off.
  • Palmwave moves ahead of XCL, whose own status line still says gameplay is not reached.

item.title: The fork drops the game's name as more builds pile onto it
item.description:
• victory-gta6 removed the game's name from its code and documents at 20:45 UTC; they now say "the title". Its address is unchanged. Take-Two's notice against Leonida had pointed to that project's explicit focus on the game.
  • The fork also merged an outside fix that lets the shaders behind its indirect lighting translate. Its README has not yet said whether shadows are now lit.
  • PortWatch lists a second private build on the fork, by a developer it calls hyphennn and shown on live streams: under player control in the opening scenes, with better lighting than other builds and no measured frame rate.
  • five-star-recomp, which has its own code, now finishes the story load and starts the opening cutscene, at under 2 frames a second.

item.title: A third build runs on the fork, at about 5 frames a second
item.description:
• PortWatch reports a private build by a developer it calls omonkey, built on victory-gta6 and shown on live streams: about 5 frames a second in the opening prison scene, with a player walking around slowly. It has no public code.
  • PortWatch now ranks victory-gta6 first among projects with public code, and calls its claim self-reported.
  • victory-gta6's README now gives 2.5 to 4 frames a second, after clean-up passes that removed about 43% of the instructions in its translated shaders.
  • five-star-recomp's story load now runs a full 300 seconds without a fault, though it does not finish. palmetto's presented frames are black, which its notes trace to textures not yet filled from the game's memory.

item.title: A second developer confirms the fork: 13 minutes of play at about 4 frames a second
item.description:
• AnyXboxX has switched to the victory-gta6 fork. Its maintainer reports playing for about 13 minutes at about 4 frames a second on an RTX 4070 SUPER, with the world on screen, the character under control and the first characters answering.
  • The session ended when the graphics device was lost, and an earlier cold start crashed while loading. The fork's own README says a device loss in its newest commits has since been traced and fixed.
  • That is the first confirmation of the fork's claim from a second machine. The fork moves to first place, ahead of the private CGBJ build, and AnyXboxX to second.
  • The time-to-playable estimate comes in by a day, to about 3 days. The one notice GitHub published since the last check concerns an unrelated project.
